review.verdict_basis: R1-R9 are resolved in source, but four new source findings remain. One is high: the pending-rekey and stale-generation write guard is dead code for the real secret-write operation. Source resolution is judged separately from final validation, which is still pending. This scoped static review makes no repository acceptance claim.

evidence: sync.rs fact_role_ok, member_removed branch: `doc["owner"] == author || is_admin(doc, author) || author == target_fp`.
is_admin requires `status == "active"`. Owner targets are still refused.

The reciprocal exception is kept only through role_document_for_removal: the author's removal set must be exactly {target}, and the fold is rerun without that author's removal. The local no-team path in membership.rs author_fact uses the same exact-set rule.
publish_fact, validate_incoming_fact (receive and pick_up_local_facts replay) and the local author_fact path all call the same predicate.

Tests: retained_admin_role_does_not_authorize_a_removed_author (predicate); removed_admin_cannot_remove_unrelated_member_on_receive_replay_or_publish; astra_team_round3 removed_by_third_party_cannot_remove_an_unrelated_admin (receive audits team_fact_not_authorized; publish fails).

new_findings.title: The pending-rekey and stale-generation write guard keys on a nonexistent op name, so real secret writes are never blocked
evidence: author_commit enters the guard only when `op["op"] == "secret.put"`, and the generation comparison checks the same name.
The only valid secret-write op is `secret.put_version`: commit.rs dispatch_validator has no `secret.put`, and share_environment emits `secret.put_version`.
So ensure_self_removal_rotations and the `team_rekey_pending` refusal never run for a real write.
The regression test submits `{"op":"secret.put"}`. That op would fail validate_ops as op_unknown, but the dead guard fires first, so the test passes without covering the production path.

Separately, the stale-generation check runs only if some generation carries removal_fact_hash. After an ordinary admin removal (rotate_dek without a hash), a version encrypted under the pre-removal generation is still accepted.
op_secret_put_version in fold accepts any known generation, not only the current one.
docs/team-sync.md §4.4 and the supplied evidence ('pending and stale-generation local writes fail closed') claim behavior the source does not have.
new_findings.impact: New shared secret versions can be encrypted under a DEK generation the removed device holds. The fail-closed boundary that confines it is absent.
resolution_conditions: Gate on `secret.put_version`. Preferably also enforce `generation_id == dek.current` for every local secret.put_version after any removal-driven rotation, or unconditionally.
Fail with team_rekey_pending while a verified self-removal lacks a completed bound rotation.

Replace the test's op with a valid, fully formed secret.put_version. Assert team_rekey_pending before rotation and success under the new generation. Assert that a stale-generation write fails after an ordinary admin removal.
Reconcile docs/team-sync.md §4.4 and the release evidence with the implemented behavior.
State whether peer-received stale-generation versions are accepted, and document that limit.

new_findings.title: The R1 fix makes member_removed acceptance depend on arrival order, which can permanently diverge membership across nodes
evidence: Authority is checked against the receiving node's current folded document, not the state when the fact was authored.
Scenario: admin X removes W, and concurrently admin Z removes X.
Node N1 receives X's fact first and accepts it, so W is removed and admins on N1 rotate the DEK away from W.
Node N2 receives Z's fact first. X is then removed, removal_authors[X] = {Z} and Z != W, so N2 rejects X's fact with team_fact_not_authorized.
send_fact_catchup on N1 replays the fact indefinitely, and N2 rejects it each time.
Facts are designed as an order-independent monotone overlay (§7.4), but W is now removed on N1 and active on N2.
The astra round-3 test covers only the after-removal ordering.
new_findings.impact: Permanent split of membership and DEK recipients between partitions; inconsistent revocation.
resolution_conditions: Define an arrival-order-independent rule that cannot be bypassed by backdating the author-controlled HLC. For example, bind facts to verifiable causal evidence.

Alternatively, document this as an explicit limit in team-sync.md §7.4 and §11. Surface rejected-but-peer-held removals in `team status`, and give admins a reconciliation step such as re-issuing the removal.
Add a two-ordering test that asserts the chosen behavior.

new_findings.title: Self-removal repair runs a full fact reload and fold on every poll, and its errors halt sync for all environments
evidence: On an admin node, poll_env (every ~50 ms) calls repair_self_removals. For every self-removal line, already-completed ones included, it re-reads facts.jsonl, runs load_facts, and folds the full commit log before checking completion.
Any error propagates with `?`. In poll it stops the remaining environments. In handle_fact it ends the receive loop and drops the session, even when the incoming fact was rejected or unrelated.
resolution_conditions: Check completion before the identity fold, and cache by fact hash.
Isolate repair failures per environment and audit them instead of aborting poll or the session.
Add a test where rotation persistently fails and other environments keep syncing.

new_findings.title: Locally appended facts that the serve process rejects remain in facts.jsonl and are applied unvalidated by load_facts
evidence: When pick_up_local_facts rejects a line, it only skips the in-memory apply. The line stays on disk.
load_facts (used by register_env after restart and by membership::load_environment in the admin CLI) applies every parseable line with no signature or authority check.
The R1 'replay' test appends an unauthorized fact and checks only the in-memory document. After a restart, or from the admin CLI's view, that member would read as removed.
Reaching this requires a local write or a CLI/serve authority disagreement. That is a write-boundary inconsistency, not a remote exploit.
resolution_conditions: Either validate signature and authority in load_facts (or at register time), or quarantine rejected local lines.
Extend the replay test to restart and to load_environment, and assert the member stays active.

non_findings_checked: Native execution in runs.rs: the session helper is resolved from the executable directory, never from PATH. The ACK listener sits in a 0700 random tempdir. If the ACK is lost, the fallback group kill targets the child pid, which cannot name the coordinator's group before setsid. Signals require pid > 1 and fall back to the process when the group kill fails. A spoofed ACK from a same-uid process cannot redirect signals to the coordinator group.
Output withholding in runs.rs: when a pump wait times out, output is empty, not unscanned. Blocked output is zeroized and replaced by a marker. On audit failure output is dropped.

Licensing: archives include MIT LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md. With bundled-openssl, openssl-src's nested OpenSSL and Text::Template notices are required. The closure excludes dev-dependencies. The Formula's license matches Cargo.toml.
install.sh: the archive entry-set check and the non-regular-entry rejection are unchanged and sound. Destination symlinks are replaced, not followed.
limitations: Static review only. Nothing was built, run or installed. Supplied evidence statements (tests passing, otool, Homebrew) were not independently verified.

Vault and CLI secret-write code, transport, incident, smtp and the fold-caller wiring were not supplied. N1's statement that every production write uses `secret.put_version` rests on commit.rs validation, which rejects any other name. How writers choose generation_id was not observed.
Homebrew semantics for `head <local path>, using: :git, revision:` and brew test sandboxing were not verified.
Cross-host gzip/zlib reproducibility and glibc portability are unverified.
This is not repository acceptance. The full macOS and Linux matrices, the bundled installed demo, and final-source Homebrew revalidation are still pending.
